gateCases.title: an authenticated participant cannot self-declare payment
gateCases.expectation: the UPDATE is refused, or payment_status/amount are unchanged

gateCases.title: a self-declared payment does not open delivery
an amount below the canonical $50 cannot be stored
a job with no briefcase item fails closed
a genuinely paid item opens delivery as zero_charge
a paid consumer packet consumes no partner credit
gateCases.expectation: one zero_charge ledger row with null entitlement and null partner

gateCases.title: repeat download requires no new payment and consumes nothing
gateCases.expectation: the ledger row count is unchanged across repeated deliveries

gateCases.title: one paid item cannot authorize a second distinct matter
gateCases.observed: second matter on the same paid item -> accounting_result=zero_charge eligibility=eligible

gateCases.title: participant B's payment cannot authorize a job for participant A
gateCases.expectation: the gate refuses a payment owned by a different participant
gateCases.observed: job bound to B's paid item -> accounting_result=zero_charge eligibility=eligible

gateCases.title: a payment-blocked job cannot record any delivery event
gateCases.observed: ERROR:  packet_delivery_events: job is not delivery-eligible

gateCases.title: a sponsored packet is not forced through the consumer gate
gateCases.expectation: consumed / eligible with a partner ledger row

gateCases.title: the sponsored packet consumed partner credit, not a consumer zero_charge
gateCases.expectation: event_type consumed against a real entitlement

gateCases.title: a schema with no consumer payment storage fails closed
gateCases.expectation: consumer_payment_required, not a crash and not a pass

mutations.title: without Phase 51 an unpaid consumer packet becomes deliverable
weakening the amount check opens a paid row carrying no amount
deleting the gate makes an unpaid packet deliverable

notes: consumer_briefcase_items has no currency column, so requirement 8's currency clause is not represented in the schema.
payment_status admits only not_applicable, unpaid, paid, refunded. pending, failed, canceled and disputed cannot be stored, so those cases are structurally unreachable rather than gated.
amount_cents carries a CHECK of 5000 or null, so a lower amount cannot be persisted at all.
Post-delivery refund behaviour is a product-policy question and is deliberately not asserted here; the pre-delivery refunded case is G3.
